chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife before he enters (consummates marriage) with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is half the dower, if he had stipulated something for her; and if he had not stipulated anything for her, then let him provide for her with a provision similar to what is provided for similar women.'

key_terms.لْيُمَتِّعْهَا: let him provide her with a gift/provision

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man's financial obligation to his wife if he divorces her before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the financial settlement for a wife divorced before consummation, distinguishing between cases where a specific dower was agreed upon versus those where it was not. In the latter scenario, the Imam prescribes 'mut'ah' (a consolatory gift) based on the husband's means and social standing, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fairness and the husband's capacity. This ruling complements the general Quranic principle by providing specific procedural guidance for the absence of a pre-agreed financial term.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorces his wife before he sleeps with her. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is half the dower, if anything was Obligated for her; and if nothing was Obligated for her, so let him provide for her upon an approximation of what similar to her from the women are provided with’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife before going to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ’He owes to her one-half of the mahr (dower) if he has set mahr (dower) for her, but if he has not set anything for her then he must benefit her in a fair manner as it is done with women similar to her.’”
